children: Adani said West Bengal’s geography could make it an integrated industrial and economic platform connecting India with Southeast Asia and beyond

Adani Group Chairman Gautam Adani on Thursday said the group expects to invest more than Rs 1 lakh crore in West Bengal by 2035, covering ports, logistics, power, roads, green cement and hyperscale data centres.

Speaking at the foundation ceremony of the Adani Arogya Mandir in New Town, Adani said the investment would support Bengal's infrastructure and economic development, while describing the state as a key link between India's industrial heartland and the Northeast.

The Adani Group is investing more than Rs 4,000 crore in the Adani Arogya Mandir, a proposed 2,000-bed not-for-profit medical institution. The facility will also include a medical college supported by advanced research and care facilities.

"Adani Arogya Mandir will be a world-class, not-for-profit medical institution that will have 2,000 beds with 1,000 beds catering to the economically vicarious section of society eligible under state and central health insurance schemes," Adani said.

Adani said the institution is expected to generate more than 10,000 jobs across the state's healthcare ecosystem. He added that the medical college and research facilities would help build a highly skilled healthcare workforce for Bengal.
Infrastructure Investment Push

The group's wider West Bengal investment programme will span ports, logistics, power generation, power transmission and distribution, roads, bridges, ropeways, green cement and hyperscale data centres, according to Adani.

"It is with this conviction that we expect to invest over Rs 1 lakh crore in Bengal over 2035 in sectors spanning ports, logistics, power generations, power transmissions and distributions, roads, bridges, ropeways, green cements and hyperscale data centres," he said.

Adani said Bengal's geography, talent and economic potential give it a structural advantage as a maritime and logistics bridge connecting India's industrial heartland and the Northeast with the Bay of Bengal.

He said, “What strengthens logistics, logistics attracts industries. Industries driving manufacturing. Manufacturing needs energy. Energy enables digital infrastructure and digital infrastructure brings in the industries of the future. And most importantly, jobs multiply.”
Adani positioned the investment commitment as part of a longer-term engagement with the state, saying Bengal could play a larger role in the group's eastern expansion.

"This morning, as I pray to Ma at Kalighat, I ask for her blessings that Bengal becomes our second Karmabhumi in the East," Adani said, referring to Mundra in Gujarat as the group's first Karmabhumi in the West.
"Because, for me, Bengal is not simply an investment destination. It is a place where I want to build to serve and, most importantly, to belong," he said.
Focus On Cultural Heritage

Alongside industrial and healthcare initiatives, Adani said the group would support the restoration of historic Writers' Buildings, revitalisation of Kumar Tuli Ghats and initiatives showcasing the art of Kolkata's Durga Puja to the world.

He said development should extend beyond infrastructure and investment, stressing the importance of Bengal's culture, memories and institutions. "A society must also care for its people and protect the culture, memories and institutions that give it identity," Adani said.
